period.measured: TSMC net revenue for AUGUST 2026, YoY vs August 2025
period.rule: the print RELEASED on the date the source text names (~2026-09-10). A Taiwan issuer announces month M's revenue by the 10th of month M+1, so the print released 2026-09-10 carries AUGUST 2026 revenue.
period.rejected_reading: 'September-2026' read as the revenue MONTH (September revenue, released ~2026-10-10)
evidence: FEASIBILITY (decisive): as_of_date is 2026-09-15. September-2026 revenue does not publish until ~2026-10-10, 25 days AFTER the claim's own resolution date. The rejected reading makes the claim structurally ungradable at the date it names; the adopted reading grades with 5 days to spare.

THE CLAIM'S OWN WORDS: both source_of_actual and the operator's seal note say '~Sept 10 2026 release'. The 2026-09-10 print is the August figure. Only the adopted reading makes the phrase and the release date agree.

THE LADDER: run_job_a._next_taiwan_prints('2026-07-27') returns ['2026-08-10','2026-09-10'] and R-WINDOW-MIX instructed the generator to 'set such a claim's as_of_date to just AFTER one of those prints'. as_of 2026-09-15 anchors to the 2026-09-10 RELEASE date — re-verified by running the helper this session.

THE CONTROL: sibling claim jobA-20260726T115635Z-C11 uses the same phrase for the OTHER reading and says so — '(~Oct 10 release)', as_of 2026-10-31. Each claim's own release date settles its own reading; the phrase alone never does.

currency.basis: New Taiwan Dollars, on BOTH sides. The threshold (0.40) anchors to cited wall TSM.revenue_estimate.0q.growth = 0.4615, which is an NT$ growth rate; the actual is the NT$ YoY the MOPS table publishes.
currency.evidence: CONFIRMED by arithmetic against live MOPS data, 2026-08-11: the wall's TSM 0q revenue avg is 1,446,809,608,550 with growth 0.46150002, implying a year-ago quarter of 989,948,401,472. TSMC's Q3-2025 revenue summed from the MOPS monthly tables (ROC 114 months 7/8/9: 323,165,707 + 335,771,691 + 330,980,920 NT$ thousands) is NT$989,918,318,000. Ratio implied/actual = 1.000030 — a match to 3 parts in 100,000. A USD reading is off by a factor of ~30 and would imply a single quarter of $1.45 TRILLION.
currency.trap_noted: The wall entry's top-level `currency` field reads 'USD' and its price is the NYSE ADR price (403.41). That field describes the PRICE, not the revenue estimate. Reading it as the estimate's currency — and therefore grading against a USD-terms YoY — would have introduced an FX error into the first resolution this record ever publishes. eps_estimate in the same entry IS USD-per-ADR (0q yearAgoEps 2.92), so a single wall entry legitimately carries three currencies at once.

source.name: Taiwan Stock Exchange Market Observation Post System (MOPS), monthly revenue announcement table
source.url_rule: t21sc03_<ROC year>_<month>_0.html, ROC year = Gregorian - 1911; the table is indexed by the REVENUE month, so August 2026 is 115_8
source.field: yoy_pct (the month's YoY revenue growth, column 7 of the MOPS row)
source.unit_handling: MOPS publishes a percentage (e.g. 44.68). It is stored as a FRACTION (0.4468) per the repo's X4 convention, which is the form match.py grades against the 0.40 threshold.
source.availability: the ROC 115_8 table does not exist yet — checked 2026-08-11, the URL returns an 869-byte stub with no rows. It publishes ~2026-09-10. assist_actual refuses it gracefully until then.

limitations: GRANULARITY: the threshold anchors to a QUARTERLY consensus growth rate (Q3-2026, confirmed by the year-ago base matching MOPS Q3-2025 exactly) while the observable measures a SINGLE MONTH's growth. August 2026 falls inside Q3-2026, so the anchor is coherent — but one month can beat or miss the quarter it sits in, and a monthly print is the noisier number. This is a property of the sealed claim, not of the reading.
The claim is SEALED-CALIBRATION: it grades on the shadow rate only and confers no ALPHA credit either way.

fields.why: TSM.revenue_estimate.0q.growth is denominated in TWD (level (.avg/.low/.high); the .growth leaf is a dimensionless RATE whose BASIS is this currency; the filer's reporting currency — NOT the quote currency)
